name: Generate tract endpoint maps
summary: Generates streamline endpoint density maps for every tract in a white matter classification (wmc), with exact, box or Gaussian smoothing of endpoints, masked to FreeSurfer grey matter.
description: Builds a grey matter mask from the FreeSurfer output and, for each classified tract, counts streamline endpoints per voxel, optionally spreading each endpoint with a box or Gaussian kernel of the given diameter, and writes the maps as NIfTI ROIs. Use it to see where tracts terminate in cortex or to make endpoint-based ROIs. The tck must be the tractogram the classification was computed on.

inputs.description: Whole-brain tractogram the classification indexes into.
inputs.requirements: Must be the tractogram used to generate the wmc classification.

inputs.description: White matter classification (wmc) assigning streamlines to tracts.
FreeSurfer output used to build the grey matter mask.

outputs.description: Endpoint density maps, one NIfTI per tract and endpoint group.

parameters.description: How endpoints are turned into density: exact endpoint voxels only, box (every voxel within the threshold distance counts as an endpoint) or Gaussian smoothing.

options.label: Exact endpoints
options.description: Make endpoint maps using only and exactly tracts' streamline endpoints

options.label: No decay
options.description: For each streamline endpoint in a tract, each adjacent mm voxel within the threshold distance is treated as though it has an endpoint in it.

options.label: Gaussian decay
options.description: An gaussian smoothing kernel is applied to each of a tract's streamline endpoints such that the density computed for each endpoint is spread in a gaussian fashion, with the kernel corresponding to the input threshold distance.

parameters.description: Odd integer values only, larger than 0.  Defines the kernel to be used if either no decay or gaussian decay is selected.  Defines *diameter* (not radius, hence odd) of smoothing kernel Ignored in the case of exact endpoints.
